# Custer County Courthouse (South Dakota)

## Basic Information

The Custer County Courthouse is located in **Custer, South Dakota**, which serves as the county seat of Custer County. The town of Custer is situated in the Black Hills region of western South Dakota.

## Historical Significance

The courthouse is listed on the **National Register of Historic Places**, having been added in 1975. This designation recognizes its architectural and historical importance to the region.

## Architectural Details

The building is an example of **Richardsonian Romanesque** architecture, a style popular for public buildings in the late 19th century. It was constructed in **1881**, making it one of the older surviving courthouses in South Dakota.

## Context

Custer County itself was established in 1875 and named after Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer, who led an expedition through the Black Hills in 1874. The courthouse has served as the center of county government for well over a century.

## Location

The courthouse is situated in downtown Custer, which is near attractions like Custer State Park and the Crazy Horse Memorial.
